t: Section 347(c) of the Maritime Transportation Security Act of 2002 (Public Law 107–295; 116 Stat. 2109) is amended by striking “within 30 months from the date of conveyance” and inserting “by December 31, 2009”.

fable.w: This section is a technical amendment that replaces one deadline with another in a conveyance provision of the Maritime Transportation Security Act of 2002. The word "conveyance" might suggest an outside party receiving property, but nothing in the text provides for consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. It only changes a date.
fable.s: is amended by striking “within 30 months from the date of conveyance” and inserting “by December 31, 2009”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific deadline in another statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative change to a date.
qwen_block.s: Section 347(c) of the Maritime Transportation Security Act of 2002 (Public Law 107–295; 116 Stat. 2109) is amended by striking “within 30 months from the date of conveyance” and inserting “by December 31, 2009”.

opus.w: This amendment only changes a deadline in an earlier statute, replacing a 30-month window with a fixed date. No outside party is consulted on, heard on, or allowed to challenge a federal decision. The word "conveyance" refers to a transfer of property, not to any participation process, so it does not cross the federal boundary as the definition requires.
opus.s: is amended by striking “within 30 months from the date of conveyance” and inserting “by December 31, 2009”
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** One tempting reading is that "conveyance" means property goes to an outside party, so outsiders are involved. That fails the definition. The amendment only replaces a deadline ("within 30 months from the date of conveyance" becomes "by December 31, 2009"). It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.
